title: When Large Language Models Confront Repository-Level Automatic Program Repair: How Well They Done?
reason: RepoBugs benchmark + RLCE, a repository-level context extraction method that supplies precise cross-file context within the prompt limit for LLM repair.

title: ExpeRepair: Dual-Memory Enhanced LLM-Based Repository-Level Program Repair
reason: Repository-level LLM repair whose contribution is context construction: retrieves past repair demonstrations (episodic) and insights (semantic) and composes them dynamically into the prompt.

title: vul-rag: Enhancing LLM-based Vulnerability Detection via Knowledge-level RAG
reason: Knowledge-level RAG that retrieves distilled vulnerability knowledge into the LLM context for vulnerability detection; context construction for code LLMs at any scope (I1), same pattern as included 2510.27675 (example selection for LLM vulnerability detection). Function-level target, so facet coding should check E4 at full text.

title: LLM-Assisted Static Analysis for Detecting Security Vulnerabilities
reason: IRIS: whole-repository vulnerability detection that combines LLMs with CodeQL. The LLM infers taint specifications that feed the static analyser (B1-like direction), and then filters paths in context. From the abstract, it is unclear whether static-analysis-selected context into the LLM is a mechanism the paper contributes.

title: Enhancing Static Analysis for Practical Bug Detection: An LLM-Integrated Approach
source_id: DOI 10.1145/3649828 (arXiv preprint 2308.00245, titled 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to Program Analysis')
reason: LLift: static analysis plus an LLM for use-before-initialization bugs in the Linux kernel. Static path analysis and post-constraint guidance appear to shape what the LLM sees across a large codebase, but the abstract does not present this as a context-construction mechanism. Needs full text.

title: LLMxCPG: Context-Aware Vulnerability Detection Through Code Property Graph-Guided Large Language Models
reason: Code-Property-Graph slice construction that compresses LLM input by 68-91% while keeping vulnerability-relevant context; it allows multi-function and project-scale analysis (a structural context-compression mechanism).
